title: SLA banding heuristic + burst reserve decision assistant for Dedicated pools
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Create a decision assistant and rubric that standardizes how we triage enterprise Dedicated capacity requests against SLA targets, sustained vs burst throughput, GPU family compatibility, and autoscaling/preemption tolerance. Goal: reduce ad-hoc gating calls, produce a predictable quota recommendation (reserved throughput + burst bucket), and emit an initial cost/latency tradeoff summary for sales and solutions. The assistant should be usable by PMs/CS/SEs during intake calls and produce a short evidence-backed recommendation (SLA band, GPU class recommendation, autoscale policy, fallback model list, estimated monthly spend). This ticket covers the rubric, implementation plan for a lightweight spreadsheet-based tool, and a first-pass exportable template for onboarding and sales decks.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page rubric that maps request signals (RPS, P95 latency target, tail percentiles, preemption tolerance, model family) to an SLA band (Gold/Silver/Bronze) and a recommended GPU family class

Spreadsheet assistant that computes: sustained vCPU/GPU minutes, reserved throughput (tokens/sec), recommended burst credits, and a 30-day cost estimate given common instance families (A100/H100/L4/T4) and quantization guidance
Playbook steps for confirmation calls: required customer telemetry, minimal benchmark prompt set, and red flags that require engineering intake
Exportable JSON/CSV summary produced by the spreadsheet that can be attached to Linear tickets and shared with sales
Sign-off from Eng runtime lead and Solutions engineering on GPU recommendations and fallback model list
notes: 2026-02-12 — Initial intake: several enterprise prospects have requested guaranteed 99th percentile latency < 150ms for generation workloads with bursts up to 3x sustained throughput. Currently we make ad-hoc decisions per request. Proposal: formalize decision tree and provide quick cost estimate.

2026-02-20 — Sync with Eng (Sofia Ruiz, Daniel Kim): Eng prefers to avoid committing H100 unless sustained utilization > 60% due to cost; suggested adding a utilization threshold and a canary rollout plan if recommending H100 for Gold SLA.

2026-02-25 — SE feedback (Priya Desai): sales needs the tool to output a clear customer-facing line item showing monthly committed cost and best-effort burst pricing. Also requested a 'graceful fallback' paragraph to hand to customers in case of region capacity issues.

2026-03-02 — Draft rubric completed and reviewed in PM sync. Key trade-offs: conservative GPU recommendations reduce NPS risk but increase price; aggressive batching/quantization recommendations lower cost but need engineering validation per model family.

2026-03-05 — Added test vectors and minimal benchmark prompt set to spreadsheet prototype. Created 'red flag' checklist: (1) multi-region strict locality, (2) air-gapped networking, (3) model non-compatibility with int8 kernels.

2026-03-09 — Eng review complete. Agreement to require a runtime performance sign-off for any recommendation that suggests aggressive quantization or novel kernel paths. Eng asks for a follow-up ticket to codify canary/rollback playbook for high-tier rollouts.
2026-03-10 — PM review: updated acceptance criteria to include exportable CSV/JSON. Next: run the assistant on 3 real inbound prospects and iterate the cost heuristics.

Action items: 1) SE to supply 3 representative customer load traces (due 2026-03-18). 2) Eng to provide validated cost-per-hour table for GPU families and common instance shapes (due 2026-03-16). 3) PM to finalize spreadsheet formulas and the handshake template for sales (due 2026-03-20).
